paragraphs: The morning begins with prospecting or client follow-up to understand needs and budgets. At midday, review plans with strategists and adjust placements and scripts. Before signing, check conversion estimates through several revisions. The afternoon brings campaign data, optimization, and renewals. Before leaving, clean up the pipeline for the month-end push.

U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) data shows about 103,700 advertising sales agents employed in 2024, falling to a projected 97,100 by 2034. That is a net loss of roughly 6,600 jobs, with about 9,300 openings each year and a 2026 median annual wage near $61,500 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace advertising sales agents, but it will reduce standardized roles. Programmatic and self-service platforms accelerate routine ad inventory, shifting sales from selling placements toward client development, custom solutions, performance optimization, and long-term relationships. People limited to standard inventory face pressure, while salespeople who develop accounts and customize solutions become more valuable.

Moderate-high exposure does not mean high risk. Standard placement selling can be replaced, not client development. People who build accounts and customize solutions become scarcer as efficiency improves. Salespeople limited to standard inventory face the greatest pressure.
